stem:
Bilal stands on soft soil in flat sandals. He then stands on the same soil in narrow-heeled shoes. His weight is the same in both cases.

Which claims about pressure on the soil are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: The pressure is greater in the narrow heels, because the same force acts on a smaller contact area.
If Bilal presses down with a larger force on the same contact area, the pressure increases.
The pressure is smaller in the narrow heels, because a smaller contact area always lowers pressure.
The pressure is the same in both cases, because his weight does not change.

teacher.key_rationale: Pressure rises when force increases or contact area decreases. Narrow heels raise pressure at the same weight; a larger downward force at the same area also raises pressure.
